headline: Brent Crude Hits $115 on Saudi Refinery Attack and Middle East Supply Fears
summary: Oil prices surged approximately $2 to reach $115 per barrel following an attack on a Saudi Arabian refinery. Geopolitical risks also intensified amid reports of a potential renewed US military campaign against Iran.
why: Crude oil is the world's most heavily traded physical commodity, and supply disruptions in the Persian Gulf directly influence global inflation and transportation costs.

impacts.name: Brent Crude
impacts.why: Prices rose following refinery damage in Saudi Arabia and heightened military threats regarding Iran.

impacts.name: Airlines
impacts.why: Higher crude prices immediately increase jet fuel operating expenses for carriers.

why_moved: Crude benchmarks climbed to $115 after an attack struck a refinery in Saudi Arabia, the world's top crude exporter, alongside heightened tensions over Iran.
